SMTO-WEB-0041 — SMTO hasn't used the browser you asked for yet

GUID: ef81f745-ab31-57a3-9951-b4285643e072
Slug: research-required-browser-not-used
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to check this with the browser, but its answer wasn't based on a page it actually viewed in the browser, so SMTO didn't accept that answer yet. What it already found is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a Capability permission required prompt appears for the Browser, select its Allow button (Allow for this conversation or Allow for this task). SMTO can't do the browser check you asked for until it's allowed to open the browser.
  2. If you don't actually need the browser, send a message saying "don't use the browser". SMTO then stops requiring a browser check and can answer from ordinary web reads.
  3. If the browser can't be used, let SMTO finish; its answer should be marked partial and say why. SMTO only accepts an answer without the browser when it openly says the browser was blocked.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's activity shows the browser reading a page, or the answer clearly says the browser check couldn't be done.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't trust an answer that claims a browser check if the activity shows no browser step.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof validation rejected the final answer because the request requires a Browser observation and the browser requirement is not satisfied (or its observation receipts no longer revalidate), and the answer is not a partial result for a blocked requirement.

What this means

  • The contract requires Browser observations and the retained method state or revalidated receipts do not satisfy that requirement; blocked partial results have a supported exception. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • The contract requires Browser observations and the retained method state or revalidated receipts do not satisfy that requirement; blocked partial results have a supported exception.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required method state and the actual retained Browser observation receipts.

How to fix it

  • Raised by validation._validate_answer when research proof validation is enabled, contract.browser_required is true and browser_requirement.status is not satisfied. Obtain an authorized browser__read_page/snapshot/find observation, or finish with status partial once the requirement is blocked; a web__read fetch alone does not satisfy it and must not be reported as a Browser observation.
  • Obtain a meaningful authorized Browser observation, or report the recorded blocker as a partial result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Obtain a meaningful authorized Browser observation, or report the recorded blocker as a partial result.

How to verify the fix

  • A meaningful authorized observation satisfies the method, or an allowed partial answer reports the blocker.

What not to do

  • Do not claim the requested Browser observation happened based on a Web fetch alone.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
